claim_29.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assays analysis of plasma from a subset of vaccinees followed through day 180 showed that antibody responses peaked at day 28 after vaccination (day 28) and declined significantly by day 180 compared to day 28.

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: The antibody responses peaked at day 28 (D28), with a significant decline in most subjects by D180 ( Figure 6A ).

claim_30.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assays analysis of plasma from a subset of vaccinees followed through day 180 showed that day 180 antibody titers depended strongly on the original day 28 response compared to subjects with lower day 28 titers.

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: Because the D180 antibody titer shows significant dependence on the original antibody response generated on day 28 ( Figure 6B ), examining the molecular profile associated with the D180 response would identify many of the mechanisms responsible for generating the D28 response.

claim_31.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assays analysis of plasma from a subset of vaccinees followed through day 180 showed that subjects with higher day 28 titers had a greater decrease in HAI response by day 180 compared to subjects with lower day 28 titers.

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: We observed that subjects with a higher D28 titer had a greater decrease in HAI response between D28 and D180, indicating increased difficulty to maintain higher levels of antibodies.

claim_32.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees followed through day 180 showed that day 7 plasmablast module activity was positively associated with day 180 antibody responses compared to subjects with lower day 180 responses.

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: As expected, correlation analysis of plasmablast module BTM S3 shows a positive association with the D180 antibody response due to the effect of D28 antibody responses, generated through plasmablast expansion ( Figure 6C ).

claim_33.claim: microarray analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees followed through day 180 showed that day 7 plasmablast module activity was not associated with the adjusted persistence of antibody responses (D180/D28 residual) compared to subjects with more persistent responses.

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: However, when we performed correlation between the plasmablast module activity and the D180/D28 residual, we no longer saw an association with the plasmablast expression ( Figure 6D ).

sources.section: Molecular Signatures Associated with the Persistence of Antibody Responses
sources.quote: Among the BTMs most enriched in subjects with a persistent response on both days 3 and 7 were several modules associated with cell movement and adhesion, such as BTM 51 ( Figure 6E ).

sources.quote: In addition, the day 7 expression of a number of T-cell-related modules was negatively associated with the D180/D28 residual, indicating that increased T cell responses might potentially result in more transient antibody responses ( Figure 6F ).

claim_40.claim: miRNA expression profiling analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 vaccinees, integrated with transcriptomic profiling, showed that day 1 miRNA expression correlated with groups of blood transcriptional modules, indicating coordinated miRNA regulation of transcriptional networks compared to modules without such correlations.

sources.section: Post-transcriptional Gene Regulation of the Immune Response to Vaccination
sources.quote: We then performed correlation analysis between all miRNA-BTM pairs, revealing groups of modules that appear to be regulated together by several miRNA ( Figure 7D ) on day 1 after vaccination.

claim_41.claim: miRNA expression profiling analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 vaccinees, integrated with transcriptomic profiling and TargetScan predictions, showed that miR-424 was a potential regulator of the day 1 antiviral interferon module M75 through predicted targeting of OAS3 and CXCL10 compared to genes not linked to this miRNA.

sources.section: Post-transcriptional Gene Regulation of the Immune Response to Vaccination
sources.quote: Of particular interest was the regulation of module M75-antiviral interferon signature ( Figure 7E ) on day 1 after vaccination, because the interferon pathway plays a key role during the innate immune response. This miRNA-mRNA network suggests potential novel regulators of the interferon response after vaccination, such as miR-424. This miRNA was predicted to target OAS3, a 2′–5′-oligoadenylate synthase involved in viral RNA degradation ( Samuel, 2001 ), as well as CXCL10, an important chemokine induced by IFN-γ that serves as a chemoattractant for lymphocytes ( Dufour et al., 2002 ).
